layout_summary: A full-height white page split vertically: a red stiletto bleeding off the left edge whose heel melts into a caramel stream that pours into a Biscoff jar occupying the lower-left column, and a four-line movie-poster serif title stack parked in the right half at mid-height. A single wide crimson caption line runs across the bottom edge, centred on the canvas.

DEVIL and BISCOFF share a right edge at x=90.5% (DEVIL 89.5%, BISCOFF 90.5% — optically flush)

THE is centred at x=57.5% — deliberately off the block centre, sitting over the D-E-V of DEVIL
The bottom caption is centred on the canvas centreline x=50% (6.9% left, 93.4% right)

scene.subject: A glossy patent-red pointed-toe stiletto pump, tilted toe-up and heel-down, cropped so its sole and toe box run off the left edge of the page; its thin stiletto heel has turned molten and pours downward as a thick caramel-brown spread that splits into three claw-like prongs and lands in the open mouth of a squat glass jar of Lotus Biscoff Smooth spread, which is overflowing — spread slumps over the rim, runs down the glass in two heavy ribbons and pools in a small blob at the lower-right of the jar base. The jar wears its own real printed wraparound label (red field with a gold wave band and biscuit imagery); no graphic layer is added to it.
scene.composition: Single left-hand column. Shoe occupies the upper third (y 10.5–45.5%), angled roughly 30° with the toe high-right and the sole exiting frame at left between y=37% and y=45.5%; its widest point reaches x=35.5% at y=25%. The melted heel runs from y=33% down to a three-pronged fork at y=48–54.5%. The jar sits bottom-left, x 14–35%, y 56–82.5%, upright and frontal, roughly 21% of canvas width. Scene and type never overlap — the shoe's right extremity (35.5%) clears the headline's left edge (47%) by 11.5%.
scene.camera: Eye-level to very slightly above the jar, straight-on frontal product view with a long-lens flat perspective (minimal convergence on the jar's cylinder). Deep focus throughout — every edge sharp, no depth-of-field falloff, no visible lens distortion.
scene.lighting: Bright, even high-key studio lighting on a pure white seamless ground. Key appears high and slightly front-left (highlight runs along the shoe's upper vamp and the left shoulder of the jar), with broad fill from the right killing almost all cast shadow — only a faint soft contact shadow under the jar base. Specular highlights are hard and mirror-like on the patent shoe, soft and waxy on the spread. Neutral-white colour temperature; no colour cast.
negative_space: Top-right field, x 36–100% / y 0–31% — the headline's breathing room
Lower-right field, x 36–100% / y 55–92% — empty white under the title stack
Full-width band x 0–100% / y 83–92% — clear run above the caption
Narrow corridor x 36–46% / y 10–83% — the gutter separating scene from type

elements.text: Don't be silly Andrea, everybody wants this.

ornaments.description: A thin black devil's-tail arrow replacing/topping the stem of the 'I' in DEVIL — it rises from the letter's apex and curves up and to the right, tapering to a solid barbed arrowhead; same black as the headline, roughly 4px stroke at its thickest

The three-pronged caramel drip forking out of the melted heel — three downward claws with pointed tips suspended just above the jar mouth (part of the rendered scene, not a graphic layer; listed because it reads as a deliberate stroke-like device)

why_it_works: Hard diagonal split: all imagery is locked into the left 35% and all type into the right 47–90%, so neither ever competes — the eye reads picture, then title, then caption with no overlap to untangle.

The melted heel is a single continuous line from the top-left corner down to the jar at 82% — it drags the eye the full height of the frame and physically connects the borrowed-icon shoe to the product.

Only two colours do any work on a pure white ground (crimson and near-black), so the red shoe at top-left and the red caption at the bottom bracket the layout and make the black title stack the sole mid-page stop.
